facts.fact: Olivia 醒来时头痛，床的另一半是空的。
facts.anchor: Olivia awoke with a sore head and empty bed.

facts.fact: 她想着除了父母和妹妹，还有谁会真的为她的消失而难过。
facts.anchor: She wondered who, apart from her parents and sister, would genuinely suffer if she disappeared.

facts.fact: Millie 打电话来找 Elliot 时，他当着 Olivia 的面眨了下眼。
她意识到自己只是填补他时间的人，等 Millie 出现他就走。
facts.anchor: She had merely been someone to fill his time until the girl he actually wanted showed up.

facts.fact: Abi 发的第三张合照把 Olivia 从中间裁掉，只剩半个她。
facts.anchor: The frame cut her down the middle, as if she was part of the background scenery.

facts.fact: Aiden Berkeley 回信说愿意回答问题，但他知道的并不比新闻多。
facts.anchor: I’d be happy to try to answer any questions you may have, but I’m not sure how helpful I can be since I don’t know much more about this tragedy than what was in the news.

facts.fact: 他提出下周来 Leeds 看朋友，可以顺便见面。
facts.anchor: However, since I happen to be coming to Leeds next weekend to visit a friend, perhaps we could meet?

facts.fact: 她发现 Aiden 的回信是在回复她自己的邮件，而那封邮件已经写完并发出。
facts.anchor: she saw his message was a reply to hers, which had, it turned out, been completed and sent.

facts.fact: 她推断是 Elliot 趁她下楼调酒时看了她写了一半的邮件，替她写完并发送。
facts.anchor: That Elliot had sneaked a look at her mad, half-written message, completed it himself and sent it.

facts.fact: 她决定在公共场所见 Aiden，以免受到伤害。
facts.anchor: She would meet Aiden Berkeley somewhere public, where he couldn’t harm her.

facts.fact: Bella 对 Elliot 的评价是“也许有点强奸犯气质”。
结尾她想起 Elliot 说过，有个室友注意到碎玻璃落在被翻乱的东西上面。
facts.anchor: She remembered Elliot’s comment, about one of the flatmates mentioning the glass from the broken window.
